summary: Rikāz refers to minerals or metals naturally occurring in the earth, like gold or silver extracted from mines. It can also mean buried treasure from pre-Islamic times.
lane: رِكَازٌ ذ Metal, or other mineral; (A, Mgh, TA;) what God has caused to exist ( رَكَزَهُ , i. e. أَحْدَثَهُ ,) in the mines; (K;) meaning تِبْر that is created in the earth; (TA;) as also : (K:) the former is pl. of : (K:) or it is pl. of : (Ahmad Ibn-Khálid, TA:) and pieces (K, TA) of large size, like [ stones such as are called ] جَلَامِيد , (TA,) of silver and of gold, (K, TA,) that are extracted from the earth, (TA,) or from the mine: (K, TA:) accord. to the people of El- 'Irák, any metals or other minerals: (TA:) or [so in the A and Mgh, and accord. to the TA, but in the K “ and, ”] buried treasure (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K) of the people of the Time of Ignorance: (S, Msb, K:) the first of the significations given above is the primary one: and ancient wealth [buried in the earth] is likened to metals or minerals: or, accord. to certain of the people of El- Hijáz, it signifies specially property buried by men before the period of El-Islám; and not metals or other minerals. (TA.) It is said in a trad., that the fifth part of what is termed رِكَازٌ is for the government-treasury: (S, * TA:) or, accord. to another relation, of what is termed : as though it [the latter] were pl. [or rather coll. gen. n.] of , or [the former] of . (TA.)
